question: What is the gestational age range that defines term labour?
explanation: Term labour typically occurs between 37 and 42 completed weeks of gestation. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T001#GNS226_U3_T001_h1)

question: Which of the following characterizes true labour contractions compared to false labour?

options.A: They are completely irregular and stop with rest
options.B: They cause progressive cervical effacement and dilation
options.C: They are painless and felt only in the lower abdomen
options.D: They disappear completely after oral hydration

explanation: True labour involves regular contractions that lead to progressive cervical effacement and dilation. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T001#GNS226_U3_T001_h1)

question: Which hormone primarily maintains uterine quiescence and relaxes smooth muscle during pregnancy?
explanation: Progesterone maintains uterine quiescence and suppresses myometrial contractions during pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T001#GNS226_U3_T001_h2)

question: What is the primary role of prostaglandins in the onset of labour?
explanation: Prostaglandins promote cervical ripening and softening by breaking down collagen fibers in the cervix. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T001#GNS226_U3_T001_h2)

question: Which pelvic shape is considered the most favorable and ideal for normal vaginal delivery?
explanation: The gynecoid pelvis has a rounded inlet and is considered the ideal shape for normal vaginal delivery. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T001#GNS226_U3_T001_h3)

question: What is the purpose of fetal head flexion during the mechanisms of labour?

options.A: To increase the presenting diameter of the head
options.B: To allow the smallest diameter of the fetal head to present
options.C: To speed up the delivery of the placenta

explanation: Flexion allows the smallest suboccipitobregmatic diameter of the fetal head to present through the birth canal. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T001#GNS226_U3_T001_h3)

question: When does the second stage of labour officially begin and end?

options.A: From the onset of contractions to 4 cm dilation
options.B: From full cervical dilation to the delivery of the baby
options.C: From the birth of the baby to the expulsion of the placenta
options.D: From placental delivery until two hours postpartum

explanation: The second stage begins at full cervical dilation (10 cm) and ends with the complete delivery of the fetus. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T001#GNS226_U3_T001_h4)

question: What is the primary clinical purpose of Active Management of the Third Stage of Labour (AMTSL)?

options.A: To accelerate cervical dilation in the first stage
options.D: To reduce the duration of the second stage

explanation: AMTSL is specifically practiced to prevent postpartum hemorrhage, which is a major cause of maternal mortality. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T001#GNS226_U3_T001_h4)

question: What is the primary function of the action line on the WHO partograph?

options.A: To indicate when the second stage of labour begins
options.B: To signal when labour progress deviates and timely intervention or referral is needed
options.C: To mark the exact time for administering pain relief medications
options.D: To show when placental separation is complete

explanation: Crossing the action line on the partograph indicates a delay in labour progress that requires intervention or referral. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T001#GNS226_U3_T001_h5)

question: Which tool is commonly used for intermittent auscultation of the fetal heart rate in low-resource settings?
explanation: The Pinard stethoscope is a traditional, reliable tool widely used for intermittent auscultation of fetal heart tones. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T001#GNS226_U3_T001_h5)

question: Which non-pharmacological comfort measure helps reduce labour pain while encouraging fetal descent?

options.A: Strict bed rest in a supine position

explanation: Upright postures and ambulation help manage pain and utilize gravity to assist fetal descent. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T001#GNS226_U3_T001_h6)

question: What is a major nursing precaution when administering systemic opioids like pethidine for labour pain?

options.C: Ensuring the mother remains in a strict Trendelenburg position

explanation: Systemic opioids cross the placenta and can cause neonatal respiratory depression if given too close to delivery. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T001#GNS226_U3_T001_h6)

question: What is the immediate nursing action when an umbilical cord prolapse is diagnosed during labour?

options.A: Encourage the mother to push forcefully with contractions
options.B: Elevate the presenting part off the cord with gloved fingers and position the mother in knee-chest
options.C: Administer oral analgesics and wait for spontaneous resolution
options.D: Perform an immediate routine vaginal examination without touching the cord

explanation: Elevating the presenting part relieves pressure on the cord, and the knee-chest position uses gravity to reduce compression. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T001#GNS226_U3_T001_h7)

question: Which maneuver is initially applied by the nurse and midwife to manage shoulder dystocia?

options.C: Placing the mother in the Trendelenburg position

explanation: McRoberts maneuver and suprapubic pressure are the standard first-line physical interventions for resolving shoulder dystocia. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T001#GNS226_U3_T001_h7)
